harmonicFunction.title: Sound Characteristics
harmonicFunction.description: Pleasant and consonant. Natural melodic movement. Stable, doesn't need resolution. Familiar "do-re" sound that is easy to sing and natural to the ear.

harmonicFunction.title: Memory Aid
harmonicFunction.description: Think of the major 2nd as the "do-re" from "Do-Re-Mi" (Sound of Music). It's the first step up the major scale and sounds natural and pleasant. Unlike the tense minor 2nd, the major 2nd feels stable and doesn't create any urge to resolve. On guitar, it's always two frets apart on the same string, making it easy to find and practice.

historicalDevelopment.title: Melodic Uses
historicalDevelopment.description: Scale construction: Primary interval in major and minor scales. Melodic movement: Natural, flowing melodic steps. Vocal music: Easy to sing and natural to the ear. Arpeggios: Connecting chord tones smoothly.

historicalDevelopment.title: Harmonic Uses
historicalDevelopment.description: Sus2 chords: Adding the 2nd degree to triads. Add9 chords: Color tones in jazz and pop. Voice leading: Smooth harmonic progressions. Polyphonic music: Independent melodic lines moving in parallel or contrary motion.

relatedIntervals.title: Melodic Major 2nds
relatedIntervals.description: Smooth Melodic Line Exercise on A string pattern
relatedIntervals.detail: Ascending: 3rd → 5th → 6th → 8th → 10th frets (C → D → E → F → G). Notice how natural and flowing this melodic movement sounds.

relatedIntervals.title: Sus2 Chord Application
relatedIntervals.description: C major to Csus2 progression: Adding the major 2nd for color
relatedIntervals.detail: The major 2nd (D) replaces the major 3rd (E) creating an open, airy sound. Move the C note (3rd fret A string) to D (5th fret A string).

relatedIntervals.title: Diatonic Scale Steps
relatedIntervals.description: Five of seven steps in the major scale are major 2nds
relatedIntervals.detail: C-D, D-E, F-G, G-A, A-B are all whole steps, making the major 2nd the most common interval in Western scales.
